- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.23) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.16 or -0.11) — model fails to account for downward pressure.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts often peak too early and then drop sharply, especially after a spike in sentiment.
- Overshoots after positive sentiment spikes — model reacts too aggressively to sentiment upturns, leading to overcorrection.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price correction — model doesn’t adjust quickly enough to true price declines, especially after sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overproject upward momentum — fails to recognize short-term volatility.
- Correction should be applied to the last 5–7 days of forecast, especially if sentiment has turned negative — model often misses the turning point.
